 ======================================================
 Appearance :
 For the Petitioners : Mr.Uday Kumar Singh, Advocate
 For the Opposite Party : Mr.Bharat Bhushan, App, 156
 ======================================================
 Coram: Honourable Mr. Justice Prabhat Kumar Singh
 Oral Order
Heard learned counsel for the petitioners, the State and the opposite party no.2.
Petitioners apprehend arrest in a case registered for the offence punishable under sections 406/420/34 and other ancillary sections of the Indian Penal Code.
As per the prosecution case, the petitioners, despite taking consideration money, neither executed sale deed nor refunded the consideration money to the opposite party no.2.
Learned counsel appearing for the petitioners submits that the petitioners are innocent and have falsely been implicated in this case.

Opposite party no.2 has not brought on record any chit of paper to substantiate the alleged payment to Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.9291 of 2023(3)
dt.19-06-2023 the petitioners.
Besides this, dispute is out and out of a civil nature.
Learned counsel for the State as well as the opposite party no.2 oppose the prayer for bail.

Learned counsel for opposite party no.2 submits that aforesaid transaction is supported by an agreement Basist Kumar Pandey @ Bashishtha Kumar ... vs The State Of Bihar on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/45644412/
1 entered into by the parties.

sentences.text: Considering the aforesaid facts of the case, prayer for bail of all the petitioners is allowed.

In the event of arrest/surrender within six weeks from today, let these petitioners, mentioned above, be enlarged on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs.10,000/- (ten thousand) each with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate VII, Gopalganj in Mahammadpur Police Station Case No. 123 of 2022, subject to the conditions laid down under section 438(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
 (Prabhat Kumar Singh, J)
